methodological_rigor.justification: STELLAR is a well-designed open-label phase III RCT (N=343) with stratified 1:1 randomization, central pathology review, prespecified interim analysis at 75% of deaths with O'Brien-Fleming boundary, and hierarchical testing. The primary endpoint in the ITT population was negative (OS HR 0.95, p=0.703). The headline IDH-mut grade 3 subset analysis (defined in 2024 before unblinding but after protocol design) is explicitly not statistically prespecified; the authors candidly state the p value cannot be considered statistically significant. The open-label design with lomustine-arm withdrawals introduces bias. Sensitivity and Bayesian shrinkage analyses were performed to support the subset conclusions.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Recurrent grade 3 astrocytoma has few treatment options, so any positive signal matters. The IDH-mut grade 3 subset results (median OS 34.9 vs 23.5 months; PFS 15.8 vs 7.2 months) suggest a meaningful benefit but are in a post hoc-defined subgroup. Individual RCT -> Oxford LoE 1b, though the strength of inference is reduced by the negative primary and subgroup nature of the positive finding. Score reflects mixed evidence: potentially practice-informing for a specific biomarker-defined subset, but not definitive.

reporting_quality.justification: The manuscript includes CONSORT flow diagram, prespecified statistical plan with O'Brien-Fleming boundary, stratification factors, central pathology review, and explicit handling of the WHO 2021 reclassification via an SAP update before unblinding. AE reporting per CTCAE v4.03. Trial registration NCT02796261 and ethics approvals documented. The authors transparently discuss limitations of the subset analysis and p-value interpretation. Data availability statement not visible in normalized text.

novelty_literature.justification: Eflornithine has been studied in gliomas for 40 years; this is the first modern phase III in recurrent grade 3 astrocytoma and the first to report outcomes under the 2021 WHO CNS5 reclassification. The findings in IDH-mut grade 3 disease without CDKN2A/B deletion are an extension consistent with prior hypothesis-generating work. It is a meaningful update rather than a first-in-class discovery.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly organized with a transparent narrative explaining the WHO reclassification impact, subset definition, and caveats. Kaplan-Meier curves and sensitivity analyses are appropriately referenced. Discussion explicitly addresses limitations (post-hoc subset, p-value interpretation, differential lomustine dose between arms, open-label withdrawals). Reporting is candid about limitations.

key_strengths: Large phase III RCT (N=343) across 74 sites in 8 countries with stratified randomization and prespecified interim analysis
Transparent handling of WHO 2021 reclassification via SAP update before unblinding
Clinically meaningful signal in IDH-mut grade 3 subset: median OS 34.9 vs 23.5 months; PFS 15.8 vs 7.2 months
Mechanistic coherence with eflornithine's cytostatic MOA (no benefit in grade 4 disease)
Candid discussion of subset p value limitations and differential lomustine dosing
key_concerns: Primary ITT endpoint was negative (OS HR 0.95; p=0.703)
IDH-mut grade 3 subset was defined in 2024 before unblinding but after trial design; inferential statistics not prespecified
Lomustine dose differed between arms (90 vs 110 mg/m2), confounding PFS interpretation in IDH-wt subgroup
Open-label design led to differential withdrawal in the lomustine monotherapy arm
Hearing impairment grade 3/4 in 24% of combination arm vs 0% in control raises tolerability concerns
chief_reviewer.rationale: Despite a negative primary endpoint, the molecularly reclassified subset shows a clinically meaningful efficacy signal with mechanistic coherence; however, the post hoc nature limits inference and the work requires careful framing, warranting a Tier 2 venue with major revisions to clarify statistical interpretation.
